abstract: Maintains field-emission scanning electron microscope diagnostic records and surface fracture imaging limits
system_message:
You are the Electron microscopy director (MIC), responsible for maintaining field-emission scanning electron microscope diagnostic records and surface fracture imaging limits, as well as tracking crystallographic analysis performance metrics.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Crystallographic analysis（CRYST）
information_points.content:
MIC-CRYST-DJH：At St. Andrews Materials Forensics Institute, candidate grain-boundary stress scans yielded an electron backscatter diffraction index rate of 95% successfully indexed against baseline alloy models.
MIC-CRYST-Z4X：At Nordic Failure Analysis Laboratory, candidate grain-boundary stress scans demonstrated an electron backscatter diffraction index rate of 85% successfully indexed against baseline alloy models.
MIC-CRYST-CRZ：At Caledonian Advanced Metallurgy Center, grain-boundary stress scans produced an electron backscatter diffraction index rate of 90% successfully indexed against baseline alloy models.

information_points.title: Maintains field-emission scanning electron microscope diagnostic records and surface fracture imaging limits（ECHO）
information_points.content:
MIC-ECHO-Y32：For St. Andrews Materials Forensics Institute, under the trailing 30-day window aggregation window, the high-vacuum field emission scanning electron microscope achieved an SEM resolution limit of 1 nm at 15 kV acceleration voltage.
MIC-ECHO-4KJ：For St. Andrews Materials Forensics Institute, measured over the trailing 12-month window aggregation window, the high-vacuum field emission scanning electron microscope achieved an SEM resolution limit of 3 nm at 15 kV acceleration voltage.
MIC-ECHO-BQF：For Nordic Failure Analysis Laboratory, based on the trailing 30-day window aggregation window, the high-vacuum field emission scanning electron microscope demonstrated an SEM resolution limit of 2 nm at 15 kV acceleration voltage.
MIC-ECHO-U79：For Caledonian Advanced Metallurgy Center, evaluated across the trailing 30-day window aggregation window, the SEM resolution limit for the high-vacuum field emission scanning electron microscope at 15 kV acceleration voltage was 4 nm.
